Chapter 10: Praying for Protection and Safety
You know, the world can feel like a risky place sometimes. That instinct to protect the people we love? It never really goes away, does it? Parents worry about accidents, about the choices their kids make, about all those unknowns out there. And as children grow up, it gets harder—sometimes impossible—to shield them from everything. That’s where prayer steps in. It’s the way we ask for what can’t be guaranteed with rules, or warnings, or even our own presence.
There’s a story about a mother whose daughter was always on the move, traveling for work. Every time her daughter planned a new trip, that familiar anxiety crept in. She’d think back to those days when she could buckle her little girl’s seatbelt, or reach out and hold her hand crossing a busy street. But now? The only thing she could do was pray—for safe travels, for smart decisions, for protection from harm.
It’s easy to overlook just how much peace comes from letting go and entrusting the people we love to something bigger than ourselves. Life’s unpredictable, and no matter how carefully we plan, we can’t prevent every danger. When parents learn to let go, they start to see that prayer isn’t about making all the risks disappear. It’s about trusting they’re not alone in their concern.
There’s also the father whose son worked a high-risk job. Every day, he’d pray—not just for safety, but for his son to stay alert, and for the right people to be close by if anything went wrong. Over time, the father realized his own anxiety was fading, replaced by a quiet confidence that he was doing everything he could.
And protection? It’s not just about physical safety. It’s about emotional and spiritual well-being too. It’s about helping our loved ones bounce back from challenges, and find wisdom to avoid harm in the first place. So, parents can pray for discernment, for courage, and for that inner voice that helps their kids recognize danger and make the best choices.
